salesops-handbook.example/close-plans#:~:text=close-date

Mutual close plans, explained

Sales Ops Handbook · 6 min read

Most forecasts treat the close date as a fact. In practice it is often a date the seller picked when the opportunity was created, and nobody on the buyer's side ever saw it.

A close date the buyer never agreed to is a hope, not a plan. Write down the remaining steps, who owns each one on both sides, and the date each must happen, then agree it with the buyer.

Teams that review slipped deals in the first week of the new quarter recover more of them than teams that wait for the next forecast call.
